clauses.mechanism: own terms: one-half-day closure and excusal limited to the single day December 24, 1947
clauses.reason: Clause 1 closes the departments and agencies one-half day on Wednesday, December 24, 1947, the day preceding Christmas Day, and excuses employees from duty; its words are "one-half day on December 24, 1947." The command is confined by its own terms to that one day, so it was performed, and exhausted, on December 24, 1947. The end is recorded as December 24, 1947, the whole day (inclusive); the exclusive reading would have the command end when that day begins, with no change in substance because the half-day closure is the performance of the command. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order. No amendment, extension or revocation is held, and the dossier chain is empty.

clauses.mechanism: performance: publication of the order in the Federal Register
clauses.reason: Clause 2 directs that the order be published in the Federal Register ("2. This order shall be published in the"). The order was published in the Federal Register issue whose date line reads "Washington, Thursday,  December 4,1947", so the direction was performed, and exhausted, on that date; it contains no continuing duty. The signature line reads "December 2, 1947." and the filing date is December 3, 1947. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order.

research_rationale:
EO 9907 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9907.txt, 12 FR 8059, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order has two numbered sections: section 1 closes the Federal agencies one-half day on Wednesday, December 24, 1947, and excuses employees; section 2 directs publication in the Federal Register. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The order's own terms confine its only substantive command to one named day.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, transfer or residual clause, and no continuing right or duty: it excused employees from duty for one-half day on December 24, 1947 only. The machine searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR and the Federal Register catalog return no hit citing EO 9907, so no held source continues any command of this order.
